messages:
alice_cust: Hey, our service started returning 401 invalid_api_key right after a nightly CI build. No code change besides the image build. Anyone seen this?

alice_cust: Quick repro — in our Dockerfile we pass the key via build-arg and write it to a file:

```Dockerfile
FROM alpine
ARG API_KEY
RUN mkdir -p /etc/myapp
RUN printf \"%b\" \"$API_KEY\" > /etc/myapp/api.key
```

Then the app reads /etc/myapp/api.key and requests to https://api.redwood.ai/v1/complete fail with 401. curl -v shows: 

```
> GET /v1/complete HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.ai
> Authorization: ApiKey <redacted>
< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
< Content-Type: application/json
{
  \"error\": \"invalid_api_key\"
}
```

alice_cust: We noticed our Vault export contains escaped sequences (e.g. `abC\\nXYZ==`) and thought printf would be safe. Is printf the problem? :thinking_face:

tess_support: Hi @alice_cust — thanks for the repro, that helps. Quick suspicion: `printf "%b"` interprets backslash escapes and will convert `\\n` into an actual newline. That changes the key bytes so the server rejects it as invalid.

lucas_dev: +1 — we hit this pattern once where a CI secret had literal `\\n` sequences (copy from a Windows-exported file). Using `%b` expands them. If the key has padding (==) it can also get split onto a new line.

alice_cust: Ahhh that makes sense. So the file ends up with a newline inside the key. Any recommended immediate fix?

tess_support: Two immediate options: 1) Change the Docker build step to preserve the raw string without expansion, e.g. `printf \"%s\" \"$API_KEY\" > /etc/myapp/api.key` — `%s` will not interpret backslashes. 2) Avoid build-arg for secrets and use Docker build secrets or mount at runtime so the secret is never re-serialized by the shell.

lucas_dev: Also check your CI variable source — if secrets were exported from Vault with `\\n` sequences, you can replace `\\n` with literal newlines only where intended. For API keys you want the literal backslash characters preserved (no expansion).

alice_cust: Tried switching to `printf "%s"` locally and rebuilt — the app auths successfully now. Rotated the key once to be safe and confirmed the new key works too.

deploy-bot: build-8463729 completed — image: prod-app:2026-03-17-09 -> now running in canary.

alice_cust: Thanks @tess_support and @lucas_dev! Leaving notes in our repo and updating CI. :white_check_mark:

tess_support: Glad that fixed it — marking this thread as resolved. If anything else crops up ping us and we can help rotate/verify. :thumbsup:
